references.text: Joseph also named his second son Ephraim, in a similar way to Manasseh, with a theological explanation tied to God's guidance through suffering.
Jacob adopted Manasseh and Ephraim as his own sons, giving them a special place among the tribes of Israel.
When Jacob blessed Joseph's sons, he placed Ephraim before Manasseh, even though Manasseh was the firstborn named in 41:51.
Joseph looks back on his suffering and recognizes God's providence - He has made him 'forgetful' of all his distress because God had a plan for everything that happened.
Moses' blessing over Joseph's tribe, which includes both Ephraim and Manasseh, shows the continuation of Joseph's sons as independent tribes in Israel.
Highlights the connection between Manasseh's status as firstborn and God's sovereign actions (here crossing hands) that break with natural order.
